prompt:
UI design mockup of the project screen of an AI software factory console, in its existing "Mission control" design: a near-black blue room (dark) or a warm cream day version (light), thin-bordered instrument panels with small corner marks, cyan as the system colour, amber as the one signal that needs a person, monospace figures, everything exact and calm. Desktop browser viewport, 16:9, flat, no browser chrome, no device frame, the screen fills the whole image.

The shell is fixed and must look like this: a quiet top bar ("Factory console", the project "ai-software-factory-code", links "Board", "New task", "Projects", "Resources", "Costs", "Policy", "Alerts", a small moon-and-sun theme selector in a thin frame, "sebastian", "Log out"); under it the pulse band, one panel with the sentence "Two cards need your decision; #612's merge carries a migration." with an amber warning sign and a 3 px amber left rule, and under the sentence the instrument strip "● waiting on you | 3 working | 2 need you | €61.40 / €120.00 ▬▬▬▭▭ 51 % | GitHub: 1 open pull request | ▾"; then the main area: the chat on the left taking 40 percent of the width as the main region, with a narrow mono table of threads at its left edge ("Inbox" first with a small house mark, "Plan: the members page" with a cyan dot, "Session store: Postgres" as the open row, "Costs read: the date window") and the open thread's log and composer at its right (the box "Ask or tell the project…", "Send", small chips "/compact" "/new", and a small level button "assisted" under Send); and the board on the right taking 60 percent with its header row "Board", a small mono text box "Find: a word, #612, plan:558", "Wide view" and "?", and four columns: "Needs you 2" lit amber (a merge approval "Merge PR #612" with chips "high risk" "migration" and buttons "Approve", "Deny", "Split"; a question "#603 Which store for the session table?" with buttons "Postgres", "SQLite", "Ask the author"), "Queued 4", "In progress 5", "Done 8", each column head with a small ▾ at its right, the cards compact with a mono state row. No ticker at the foot.

What is new, and what this image is about: the member reads the project's documents inside this screen, Markdown files from the project's git repository, and moves between them by their links without leaving the chat. The open document is "docs/roadmap.md", rendered as readable text in the console's type at a comfortable measure, never as code: the heading "The project screen and members", then three numbered items as paragraphs, spelled exactly: "225. The lanes collapse: no card is filed undecided." with an underlined cyan link "the plan" inside the paragraph; "263. The backlog pull and the close-out." with the link "the plan" and the line "Where it stands: planned, the plan, not built."; "205. The main loop keeps the roadmap and its working notes." The document's head shows its path "docs/roadmap.md" in small mono, a two-way switch "Read | Edit" with Read pressed, a small "Open in Forgejo ↗" link, and a small "New document" button. The linked plan, where a direction shows it, is "docs/plans/2026-10-15-backlog-pull-and-close-out.md" with the heading "Plan: the backlog pull and the close-out". Where a direction shows the edit state, it is the same document as raw Markdown in a plain text area in mono, with a "Save as commit" button and the quiet line "Saved: 9e6bb40 on master · 14:12". The chat at the left stays as it is and stays usable: the member copies between the document and the chat.

Direction "Split": The drawer is open at the board's full 60 percent width over the board, and the chat stays at the left. The drawer is split into two equal panes by a hairline: the left pane holds the roadmap, the right pane holds the linked plan "Plan: the backlog pull and the close-out", each pane with its own small head (the path in mono, "Read | Edit"). A link clicked in the left pane opens its target in the right pane, so the source and the target are side by side. Over both panes one row: "Swap ⇄", "One pane", "Open in Forgejo ↗", "New document", ×. The left pane's link "the plan" on item 263 is shown in the pressed state (a faint cyan background) to say it is the one open at the right. Light theme: the cream day version of the same design, dark navy text on warm off-white panels, the same cyan and amber.

Legible UI text with exact spelling, nothing invented, no lorem ipsum. The pulse stays the loudest thing on the screen after the amber Needs you column; the chat stays the main region; the document is a quiet reading surface in the text colour, its links the only cyan in it, and the only loud marks are the ones the shell already has. Made by a top product design studio. Not a template, not a generic admin dashboard, not a code editor.
